structure_note: The high number of printed repeats (143) and backsteps (33) likely reflects misread manuscript foliation numbers rather than actual structural defects. There is also a small discrepancy between pages with OCR (507) and pages translated (503).
reader_summary: A reader of this tradition will find a 14th-century manuscript containing classical Greek tragedies and poetry. However, the Greek transcription is severely corrupted by hallucinations that replace the actual text, as well as rampant XML tag leakage. Consequently, the English translation reflects these errors and missing passages, making the text completely untrustworthy.
book_verdict: The pipeline fails on this manuscript, with the transcription model hallucinating Greek text, dropping passages, and leaking XML tags and English image descriptions into the reader pane. These severe errors cascade into the translation, rendering the book unreadable.

title: Vitruvii de architectura libri X
shelf_note: A 13th-century Latin manuscript of Vitruvius fits the Greek and Latin classics tradition.
structure_note: The 18 printed backsteps and 14 repeats out of 116 pages likely reflect misread folio numerals or unnumbered versos typical of manuscript foliation.
reader_summary: This is a scan of a 13th-century Latin manuscript of Vitruvius. The transcription is heavily polluted with leaked XML tags, English image descriptions, and model reasoning masquerading as text. The English translation is untrustworthy, dropping large sections, hallucinating sentences from garbled OCR, and substituting Arabic flyleaf text with invented editorial notes.
book_verdict: While the manuscript fits the collection, the extraction pipeline has failed catastrophically on it. Rampant XML tag leakage, model reasoning printed as source text, and highly defective translations render the presentation unusable.
